content: How to Use This Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for your specific needs. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your individual health requirements. Uses: Posaconazole is prescribed to prevent certain fungal infections in individuals with severely weakened immune systems, such as those undergoing chemotherapy. It belongs to a class of medications known as azole antifungals. How to Use: Before starting posaconazole, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist, and review it again each time you receive a refill. This medication is administered via injection into a vein, typically once daily, as directed by your doctor. If you are administering this medication at home, ensure you have been thoroughly trained by your healthcare provider on how to prepare and use it correctly. Before using the medication, visually inspect it for particles or discoloration. Do not use the liquid if either is present. For optimal effectiveness, maintain a consistent level of the medication in your body. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, abdominal pain, dizziness, or difficulty sleeping. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, posaconazole has been associated with severe (and potentially fatal) liver disease. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are also rare. However, posaconazole can commonly cause a mild rash, which is usually not serious. Be aware that it may be difficult to distinguish a mild rash from a rare rash that could indicate a severe allergic reaction. This is not a comprehensive list of side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance on side effects. Precautions: Before using posaconazole, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other azole antifungals (such as ketoconazole), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Posaconazole may cause a condition that affects heart rhythm, known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other medications that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can also increase your risk of QT prolongation. This risk may be heightened if you are using certain drugs (such as diuretics or water pills) or if you experience conditions like severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. If you use marijuana, discuss this with your doctor. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect the removal of posaconazole from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Similarly, posaconazole can slow the removal of other drugs from your body, which may affect how they work. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Notes: Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as kidney and liver function tests, and blood mineral levels like calcium, magnesium, and potassium) should be conducted before starting this medication and periodically while using it. Attend all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. Missed Dose: It is important to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately to establish a new dosing schedule. Storage: Refer to the product instructions and consult your pharmacist for specific storage details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Reminder: This document is a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
